axis: Chat shells and app shells — parallel implementations of the main screen
summary: Three of the four historically-parallel web chat implementations have already collapsed to one live copy: WebChatPage.tsx (~4,565 lines) is mounted three ways (/, /chat via WebChatRoot; /chat/[sessionId] via a second, independent dynamic-import wrapper). The fourth — UnifiedChatPage.tsx → WebShellV3.tsx → ChatInterface — is confirmed, triple-corroborated dead code (zero real importers; self-documented as "kept internal, do not expose"; already listed in scripts/config/surface-reachability-allowlist.json; independently flagged dead by two other same-day audit passes). The real live risk is one layer down, in the primary left-nav rail: three separate implementations of "the sidebar" coexist — the shared @agiworkforce/ui <Sidebar> wired independently (with hand-duplicated CRUD handlers) in both WebChatPage.tsx and WebAppShell.tsx, and v3's structurally distinct WebSidebar.tsx, which escaped its dead parent shell and is the ONLY rail CloudCodePage.tsx (the live, nav-linked /chat/code route) renders — with its own hardcoded nav-item list that visibly diverges from the rest of the app's rail (it shows "Desktop app"/"VS Code extension" instead of Chat/Code/Projects/Artifacts/Library/Tasks/Schedules/Customize). The nav-items half of the WebChatPage/WebAppShell split was just unified today via a new app-nav-items.ts (untracked in git status); the CRUD-handler duplication and the v3-sidebar escape were not touched and remain live risks. A materially complete, fully-built multi-format (Markdown/PDF/DOCX) export dialog is stranded, unreachable, inside the dead v3 cascade.

duplicates.what: Full chat-surface implementation (page + shell + sidebar + empty state + search modal, wrapping packages/ui/unified-chat's ChatInterface)
duplicates.liveCopy: none — apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx is what every real route (/, /chat, /chat/[sessionId]) mounts instead
duplicates.evidence: grep -rn "UnifiedChatPage" apps/web (excl .next) returns only a vi.mock in chat-route.test.tsx:36-37 and a doc-comment in web-chat-store.ts:6 — zero real imports. No app/**/page.tsx imports UnifiedChatPage or WebShellV3. app-nav-items.ts:101-103 (live file) already calls it 'a dead shell (WebShellV3, zero mount points)'. UnifiedChatPage.tsx:49-54 self-documents 'kept internal ... do not expose a second public chat route.' scripts/config/surface-reachability-allowlist.json:303-318 already lists this file plus ~10 sibling files (use-export-conversation.ts, conversation-export.ts, document-export.ts, EnhancedExportDialog.tsx via dialogs/index.ts, etc.) as accepted unreachable debt. Two independent same-day audits (audit/parity-2026-08-15/gaps/domain-dead-code.json:164-219, audit/competitive-gap-2026-08-15/fixes/01-web-chat-shell.json:8) reach the identical conclusion.
duplicates.driftRisk: Low for the shell itself (unreachable, so users never see divergence) but real for the code hiding inside it: WebChatRuntime.ts injects memory with no isTemporary guard that the live request-processor.ts:976-996 path has (per audit/parity-2026-08-15/gaps/domain-memory.json:205-215) — a privacy gap that would ship silently if this were ever wired up 'for free'. A fully built multi-format (MD/PDF/DOCX) EnhancedExportDialog.tsx is completely unreachable while live WebChatPage.tsx ships only Print.
duplicates.recommendation: Delete the cascade (UnifiedChatPage.tsx, WebShellV3.tsx, WebEmptyChat.tsx, WebSearchModalCmdK.tsx, WebChatRuntime.ts, WebSidebar.test.tsx, WebShellV3.navigation.test.ts, the export dialog/hooks/services) once WebSidebar.tsx and resolveWebViewRoute are extracted for their live consumer (see next entry). Re-home EnhancedExportDialog + conversation-export.ts + document-export.ts onto the live WebChatPage.tsx header first rather than deleting a working feature.

duplicates.what: Left-nav-rail session/project CRUD handler wiring (delete/rename/pin/star/archive conversation; open/new-chat/settings/pin/delete/create project) around the shared @agiworkforce/ui <Sidebar> primitive
duplicates.liveCopy: both, simultaneously — WebChatPage.tsx for /chat and /chat/[sessionId]; WebAppShell.tsx for /chat/projects, /chat/projects/[id], /chat/library, /chat/artifacts, /chat/schedules, /tasks
duplicates.evidence: WebAppShell.tsx:14-16 states the duplication is deliberate ('intentionally NOT refactored onto this shell'). WebAppShell.tsx:229-232 admits the delete-conversation dialog copy is 'Same dialog and same copy the chat shell uses' — matched by hand today (WebChatPage.tsx:2997-3000 vs WebAppShell.tsx:171-176 have identical strings, with nothing enforcing that). The sibling duplication of the nav-ITEMS array already drifted once (app-nav-items.ts:1-19: /chat rendered 6 entries, /chat/library rendered 7, Tasks was missing from chat, isActive was hardcoded wrong) and was fixed only today — app-nav-items.ts is untracked in `git status --short`. The CRUD-handler duplication this entry describes was not touched by that fix.
duplicates.driftRisk: A fix to delete-conversation guard logic, archive semantics, or dialog copy in one file has no mechanism forcing the same change into the other — demonstrated by the nav-items array already drifting once under the identical pattern.
duplicates.recommendation: Extract a shared useSidebarSessionActions() hook returning the handler set both files build individually, mirroring the buildAppNavItems() extraction just done for nav items.

duplicates.what: Primary left-nav rail component — a third, structurally independent implementation (own conversation grouping, own hardcoded per-mode nav-item table, own markup) that does not use the shared @agiworkforce/ui <Sidebar>
duplicates.liveCopy: apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx imports WebSidebar and resolveWebViewRoute directly (CloudCodePage.tsx:29-30, mounted at CloudCodePage.tsx:277) for the live, nav-linked /chat/code route — even though WebSidebar's designed home, WebShellV3.tsx, is dead (see first entry)
duplicates.evidence: grep -rln "features/chat/v3/WebSidebar" apps/web returns only WebShellV3.tsx (dead), WebSidebar.test.tsx, and CloudCodePage.tsx (live). app-nav-items.ts:76-153 documents APP_NAV_DESTINATIONS as 'the rail ... every signed-in surface shows all of these' (Chat/Code/Projects/Artifacts/Library/Tasks/Schedules/Customize), but WebSidebar.tsx:103-107's navItemsForMode('code') returns only [{'Desktop app'},{'VS Code extension'}] — a completely different item set, different icons, no shared <Sidebar> at all. CloudCodePage.tsx:275 also builds its own shell div instead of using WebAppShell, a fourth chrome pattern.
duplicates.recommendation: Migrate /chat/code onto WebAppShell + buildAppNavItems like every other secondary route before deleting the rest of the v3 cascade. Once that migration lands, WebSidebar.tsx and resolveWebViewRoute have zero live consumers and can be deleted as part of the Finding-1 cleanup. Do not delete WebSidebar.tsx as part of a blanket 'delete v3' pass without doing this migration first — it is the only thing currently rendering the /chat/code rail.

duplicates.what: Two independent dynamic(() => import(WebChatPage), {ssr:false, loading}) wrappers with two different cold-load skeletons
duplicates.liveCopy: both — same underlying WebChatPage.tsx, different loading fallback depending which of the three routes is hit first (WebChatRoot's inline WebChatSkeleton spinner vs. [sessionId]'s reuse of the segment's ChatLoading)
duplicates.evidence: WebChatRoot.tsx:6-11 and app/chat/[sessionId]/page.tsx:6-11 carry near-identical 'GOV-25' comments describing the same fix applied by hand in two files, each declaring its own dynamic() call with a different loading component.
duplicates.recommendation: Low priority, cosmetic only. Route [sessionId]/page.tsx through WebChatRoot, or share one loading component between both wrappers so cold-load looks identical across all three entry points.

duplicates.what: GalleryClient mounted twice — /gallery (public marketing chrome) and /chat/artifacts (in-app WebAppShell chrome)
duplicates.liveCopy: both, deliberately — /gallery for signed-out/SEO, /chat/artifacts for the in-app rail
duplicates.evidence: Both routes render the same GalleryClient component with a chrome prop ('public' vs 'app'); app/chat/artifacts/page.tsx sets robots: {index:false} and alternates.canonical: '/gallery' so search engines see one canonical page, and its comment (lines 6-24) explains exactly why /gallery can't simply move into the app shell (must stay reachable/indexable signed-out).
duplicates.driftRisk: None beyond the ordinary maintenance cost of one component — this is the exact 'public SEO page + in-app page sharing one component' pattern called out as deliberate in the audit brief.
duplicates.recommendation: No action — included as a contrast case since the founder specifically named 'gallery' as a suspect.

axis: Library / Artifacts / Gallery — "my generated stuff" surfaces
summary: The founder's suspicion is half right. `/gallery` and `/chat/artifacts` are NOT duplicated code — they mount the literal same `GalleryClient` (one import, verified by a regression test), which is a deliberate public-SEO-page / in-shell-page split. The real finding is elsewhere: the Artifacts gallery (Claude-style, dedicated) and Library (ChatGPT-style, unified) are both genuinely live, both linked as sibling primary-nav entries, and both explicitly justified as deliberate in code comments — but they read from three disconnected backing stores (browser localStorage for chat-derived artifacts, a one-way Desktop-to-Web `web_artifacts` pull, and a durable server-side `media_assets` table for tool-generated files) with zero bridge between them. An HTML artifact born from a chat fenced-code-block never reaches Library; an HTML file born from a code-execution tool never reaches the Artifacts gallery's rich preview, even though the backend already classifies it as `surface: 'artifact'`. The Artifacts gallery's own nav comment claims it is "account-scoped," which is false for web-originated content — that mismatch, not the two-icon nav layout, is the actionable bug.

duplicates.what: Artifacts gallery page mounted twice (public marketing route + in-shell route)
duplicates.liveCopy: both — /gallery for signed-out/SEO traffic, /chat/artifacts for the signed-in primary-nav rail
duplicates.evidence: apps/web/app/chat/artifacts/page.tsx:4 imports GalleryClient from '@/app/gallery/GalleryClient' — the exact same file, no fork. apps/web/app/chat/artifacts/page.test.tsx:10-31 asserts this explicitly ('Not a forked copy of the gallery'). metadata.robots={index:false} + alternates.canonical='/gallery' fences SEO correctly. apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.ts:100-119 routes the rail to /chat/artifacts specifically so signed-in users stay inside WebAppShell.
duplicates.driftRisk: None — single source, a fix to GalleryClient lands on both routes automatically, and a test guards the invariant.
duplicates.recommendation: No action needed. Keep as-is.

duplicates.what: "Things the user generated" modeled as two disconnected products: a dedicated Artifacts gallery (Claude-pattern) and a unified Library (ChatGPT-pattern), both live, both on the primary nav rail, with no shared storage or cross-linking
copies: apps/web/features/chat/services/artifact-cloud-sync.ts + apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts (web_artifacts table, Desktop-authored artifacts, pull-only on web)
duplicates.liveCopy: both surfaces are live and reachable; neither is dead. The data underneath is what's fragmented, not the UI.
duplicates.evidence: app-nav-items.ts:101-112 explicitly frames Artifacts as 'Claude parity... not one row inside a generic Library' beside Library's 'ChatGPT-Library... parity of concept' comment — a documented, intentional product split. But: artifacts-store.ts's addArtifact/upsertArtifact (lines 493-570) make zero network calls — persistence is localStorage only (line 335-362 quotaAwareArtifactStorage). use-artifact-cloud-sync.ts pulls web_artifacts one-way (Desktop/Mobile push via packages/client/sync; web has no push implementation — grep for POST to /api/chat/sync from web found none) and resets to an in-memory-only overlay every mount (comment: 'starts from cursor zero for each authenticated mount'). Meanwhile generated-file-persist.ts:156-180 classifyGeneratedFile already buckets html/svg/md/mermaid/json/code into surface:'artifact' inside media_assets — the exact taxonomy that could unify the two — but LibraryView.tsx renders every row (including surface:'artifact') through the plain GeneratedFileCard (download/open-in-new-tab), never through the rich ArtifactPreview (sandboxed iframe, versions, iterate) that /chat/artifacts and the in-chat ArtifactsPanel use.
duplicates.recommendation: Do not merge the two surfaces into one screen — they answer genuinely different questions (durable searchable history vs. live editable/versioned artifact) and merging would just reproduce ChatGPT's pattern without ChatGPT's unified storage. Instead: (1) stop claiming the Artifacts gallery is 'account-scoped' in code/product copy until it is, or make it true by adding the missing web-side push to web_artifacts (the POST /api/chat/sync artifacts array already exists server-side); (2) render Library rows with surface:'artifact' through ArtifactPreview instead of GeneratedFileCard, and/or link them into the Artifacts gallery, so tool-generated HTML/SVG/Markdown gets the same rich viewer chat-derived artifacts get.

duplicates.what: In-chat docked Artifacts side panel vs. the cross-conversation Artifacts gallery
duplicates.liveCopy: both — different scope, not competing
duplicates.evidence: ArtifactsPanel.tsx filters via getConversationArtifacts(activeConversationId) (conversation-scoped, auto-opens on new artifact) vs. GalleryClient's full cross-conversation grid with tabs/search. Both read the same useArtifactsStore and both delegate final rendering to the same ArtifactPreview component (ArtifactsPanel.tsx:16, GalleryClient.tsx:8-9) — confirmed no forked renderer.
duplicates.driftRisk: None found — shared store, shared renderer component.
duplicates.recommendation: No action needed.

duplicates.what: Peripheral 'artifact' surfaces that sound like galleries but aren't: marketing feature page, public share-token view, dev QA harness, settings revoke-list
duplicates.liveCopy: features/artifacts and shared-artifact/[token] are live and correctly scoped; qa-artifacts is dead in production by design
duplicates.evidence: features/artifacts has no data fetch, just prose (linked from MarketingFooter.tsx:41, MarketingLanding.tsx:226) — sells the capability, doesn't browse it. shared-artifact/[token] reads a 4th table (published_artifacts via app/api/artifacts/publish, migration 0095) and is only reachable via a minted token link. qa-artifacts/layout.tsx calls notFound() under NODE_ENV=production, the dir is gitignored (.gitignore:246), and it's in robots.ts DISALLOW_APP — unreachable by real users. PublishedArtifactsSection.tsx explicitly mirrors SharedLinksSection as a privacy revoke-list, not a browser.
duplicates.driftRisk: qa-artifacts carries a stale 'Delete after QA' comment in its own header — harmless (inert in prod) but worth a housekeeping pass.
duplicates.recommendation: No functional action needed; optionally delete apps/web/app/qa-artifacts now that its QA purpose is served, per its own comment.

axis: Tasks vs Schedules vs Work sessions — overlapping async-work surfaces
summary: A Task, a Schedule run, and an AGI Work session are three genuinely different backend objects on web (cloud_agent_runs with a full tool-using agent harness; scheduled_tasks/scheduled_task_runs with a capped single-shot completion and no tools; and an ephemeral client-side projection of a Task's live SSE stream) — not one concept wearing three names, and the Schedule form is honest in its own copy about lacking tools/research/media. But they are presented as two unrelated, cross-link-free top-level nav destinations rather than the one-list-with-a-split pattern the benchmark found in competitors, and today's uncommitted app-nav-items.ts fix shows Tasks was completely unreachable until now, which is evidence this area has been actively drifting. The real code-level duplication is on Desktop: Local mode shows the identical scheduled-jobs list (same useSchedulerStore) through two independently hand-coded renderers reachable from two different nav paths, a fully dead 'legacy job-based' scheduler subsystem sits unimported next to the live one, a fourth BackgroundTasksPanel task-list UI is mounted nowhere at all, and web's in-chat WorkSessionPanel duplicates TaskDetailPanel's entry-to-row mapping logic for the same run instead of sharing one projector on top of the already-shared applyAgentActivityEvent reducer.

duplicates.what: Desktop Local-mode 'scheduled tasks' list (device-owned, useSchedulerStore)
duplicates.liveCopy: both — AgiWorkScheduled is the top-level Sidebar 'Scheduled' destination (Sidebar.tsx:163, DesktopShellV3.tsx:879-880); ScheduledTasksPanel is the 'scheduled' tab inside AgentTaskPanel, itself the top-level Sidebar 'Tasks' destination in Local mode (DesktopShellV3.tsx:843-848, AgentTaskPanel.tsx:7)
duplicates.evidence: AgiWorkScheduled.tsx:59-63 and ScheduledTasksPanel.tsx:44-47 both call useSchedulerStore((s) => s.tasks) — same store, same data — but render independent row markup (custom iOS-toggle rows vs ScheduledTaskCard, ScheduledTasksPanel.tsx:179). Both call the same CreateTaskModal to create a task (AgiWorkScheduled.tsx:6,168; ScheduledTasksPanel.tsx:9,186), confirming the write path is meant to be shared while the list-render path was not.
duplicates.recommendation: Route the top-level 'Scheduled' nav item to render ScheduledTasksPanel/ScheduledTaskCard directly (more complete: supports edit) instead of AgiWorkScheduled's parallel markup, eliminating both the duplicate renderer and the confusing appearance of 'Scheduled' as its own nav item AND a sub-tab of 'Tasks'.
duplicates.driftRisk: A status/label fix applied to ScheduledTaskCard (e.g. how a paused job displays) will not reach AgiWorkScheduled's inline markup, so the two nav paths to 'my schedules' can show different states for the same job.

duplicates.what: Desktop 'legacy job-based' scheduler UI (SchedulerPanel, JobCreationDialog, useScheduler hook)
duplicates.liveCopy: none
duplicates.evidence: scheduler/index.ts:7-15 self-labels this half of the directory '// Legacy job-based system (kept for backwards compatibility)' vs '// Task-based system (actively used)' for ScheduledTasksPanel/CreateTaskModal. grep -rln for SchedulerPanel/JobCreationDialog outside features/scheduler/ returns zero hits; grep -rln for the barrel import '@/features/scheduler' anywhere in the app also returns zero hits — every live consumer imports ScheduledTasksPanel/CreateTaskModal directly by path.
duplicates.recommendation: Delete SchedulerPanel.tsx, JobCreationDialog.tsx, and the useScheduler hook after a one-time check that no Tauri #[tauri::command] (scheduler_*_job) exists solely for their benefit.
duplicates.driftRisk: None currently (inert), but it is an active confusion trap for future contributors searching for 'the scheduler panel' and a stale comment implying compatibility work that isn't happening.

duplicates.what: Desktop 'background tasks' list UI (BackgroundTasksPanel / BackgroundTaskIndicator)
duplicates.liveCopy: none
duplicates.evidence: grep -rln 'BackgroundTasksPanel|BackgroundTaskIndicator' across apps/desktop/src outside features/background-tasks/ returns zero hits — no nav entry, no panel-switch case, no toolbar mount anywhere in DesktopShellV3.tsx or elsewhere.
duplicates.recommendation: Confirm whether the backing store (useBackgroundTasks / BackgroundTask in stores/chat/agentStore.ts) still has a live producer; if nothing writes to it either, delete the whole vertical. If something still writes to it with no UI reader, that is a half-wired feature per repo policy and belongs in PLAN.md/known-flaws.md rather than silent dead UI.
duplicates.driftRisk: None currently; the risk is a fourth 'task' concept (BackgroundTask) existing in the type system alongside the three that are actually wired up (CloudAgentRun, AgentTaskStore goal, ScheduledTask), compounding the object-model confusion the founder is asking about.

duplicates.what: In-chat live AGI Work progress view vs the /tasks durable run detail view, for the same run
duplicates.liveCopy: both, simultaneously, for the same underlying CloudAgentRun — WorkSessionPanel while the originating chat tab is open (WebChatPage.tsx:4489-4493), TaskDetailPanel whenever /tasks or Desktop Tasks is open (TasksPage.tsx:567-584)
duplicates.evidence: Both consume the same AgentActivityEntry/AgentActivityState shape built by the shared reducer applyAgentActivityEvent (packages/client/client-runtime/src/agentActivity.ts) — useChat.ts uses it live while streaming, TaskDetailPanel.tsx:56-61 (projectTaskJournal) uses it to replay the durable journal. But the entry-to-row mapping is hand-duplicated: WorkSessionPanel.tsx:150-158 (progressFromActivity) has a legacy message.metadata.tools fallback branch (WorkSessionPanel.tsx:258-274) that TaskDetailPanel has no equivalent of; WorkSessionPanel falls back to humanizeToolName(entry.name) when summary is empty (WorkSessionPanel.tsx:154) while TaskDetailPanel.tsx:95 uses entry.summary || entry.name with no humanizing — the same tool call can render differently in the two surfaces. Status/tone-to-color mapping is also independently coded in each (WorkSessionPanel.tsx:100-107 inline classes vs TaskDetailPanel's TASK_TONE_BADGE_CLASS table).
duplicates.recommendation: Extract one shared entry -> {label, detail, status, tone} projector (natural home: next to applyAgentActivityEvent in client-runtime, since both sides already depend on that package) and have both components call it instead of maintaining parallel switch statements.
duplicates.driftRisk: A fix to how a tool/progress entry is labeled or toned has to be applied in two places or the live in-chat panel and the /tasks detail panel silently disagree about the same event for the same run.

duplicates.what: Web Tasks (/tasks, cloud_agent_runs) and Schedules (/chat/schedules, scheduled_tasks) as two unrelated primary-nav lists instead of one automation surface
duplicates.liveCopy: both — both are real, separately reachable rail destinations in apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.ts:138-152, each backed by a fully working, non-overlapping end-to-end system
duplicates.evidence: Schedules execute a capped single-shot completion with explicit no-tools disclosure in the form itself (ScheduleForm.tsx:110-113: 'Web search, tools, research, files, and media generation are not available in this surface'), via scheduled-agent-executor.ts:49-90, writing only to scheduled_task_runs — never to cloud_agent_runs (apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql vs 0057_durable_scheduling.sql/0009_scheduling.sql show no FK or shared row between the two table families). grep for 'schedule' inside the Tasks components and for '/tasks'/'cloud_agent_run' inside the Schedules components both return zero cross-links in either direction. A user cannot schedule a tool-using AGI Work run at all, only a plain-text one, despite 'Schedule' sitting in the nav next to 'Tasks' (whose own empty-state copy says runs from AGI Work show up there).
duplicates.recommendation: Not a code merge: either cross-link the two surfaces (a Task shows which schedule spawned it once that's technically possible; a Schedule's run row links to its Task if one exists) or extend scheduled execution to optionally use the full agent harness so a unified Active/Scheduled/History list becomes meaningful. Treat as a product/scope decision, not a refactor — do not visually merge the lists before deciding whether scheduled runs should gain tool access.
duplicates.driftRisk: Not code drift (no shared implementation exists to diverge) — a product-legibility risk: the vocabulary overlaps (Task, ScheduleTask, AgentTaskStore, ScheduledTask are four distinct types surfaced in this audit) so the user's 'one place for my automated work' mental model from every competitor is violated by two silently disconnected systems.

axis: Duplicated components — same UI built more than once (library, artifacts, gallery, and the chat shell that causes most of it)
summary: The founder is right, and the mechanism is bigger than isolated copy-paste: web never cut over to the shared chat shell (ChatInterface in packages/ui/unified-chat) that desktop already runs on daily. Web's adapter for it, UnifiedChatPage.tsx, is fully built and tested but is explicitly locked out by a regression test asserting the real /chat route always renders web's own 4,565-line WebChatPage.tsx instead — and known-flaws.md independently confirms this as an "orphaned, unrouted duplicate implementation." That single fork is the root cause of the founder's MessageBubble finding (web's own vs. unified-chat's, live only for desktop) and forces a shadow ArtifactPanel too. Separately, desktop built its own "AgiWork*" gallery family (AgiWorkArtifacts, AgiWorkProjects) instead of reusing the shared package's equivalents, and left behind a fully-built 580-line ArtifactsGallery.tsx with zero importers anywhere. By contrast, Library and the public/in-app Gallery page are done correctly — one shared implementation, documented thin adapters — proving the codebase knows how to avoid this when it tries.

duplicates.what: MessageBubble (chat message renderer)
duplicates.liveCopy: web: apps/web's own copy (via WebChatPage.tsx -> ChatMessageList.tsx); desktop: packages/ui/unified-chat's copy (via DesktopShellV3.tsx -> ChatInterface, desktop_chat_v3 flag defaults enabled:true); mobile: its own React Native copy
duplicates.evidence: apps/web/app/chat/page.tsx -> WebChatRoot -> WebChatPage.tsx:109 imports ChatMessageList which imports the web-local MessageBubble; apps/desktop/src/features/v3/DesktopShellV3.tsx:749 mounts <ChatInterface>, whose internal message list uses unified-chat's own MessageBubble; sizes diverge ~2250 vs ~925 lines confirming independent maintenance, not a thin wrapper; a code-block copy-button hover-gate bug was fixed today only in the shared markdown renderer.
duplicates.driftRisk: A behavior or bug fix landed in one MessageBubble (as already happened today with the copy-button fix) does not reach the other; there is no shared core, so every future UX change to message rendering must be manually ported twice for web+desktop parity. Mobile's separate copy is a genuine React Native vs DOM platform constraint, not drift.
duplicates.recommendation: Not fixable by deleting a file alone — depends on resolving the chat-shell duplication finding below (web cutting over to ChatInterface). Until then, treat both copies as permanently forked and require every behavior fix to be applied to both explicitly.

duplicates.what: MessageMetadata TypeScript interface
duplicates.liveCopy: apps/web/shared/stores/web-chat-store.ts (imported by apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts, the live send/persist path, and by MessageBubble.tsx aliased as StoreMessageMetadata)
duplicates.evidence: web-chat-store.ts:164 declares fields like privacyMode/providerMode/handoffDraftId; shared/types/common.ts:86 declares a disjoint set including employeeId/employeeName/thinkingProcess; shared/stores/unified-chat-types.ts:20 declares another disjoint set including tokenCount/widgets/taskId, imported by useSessionPersistence.ts and sessionStorage.ts. Three real, independently-evolved interfaces sharing one name, not copies of one shape.
duplicates.driftRisk: Adding a field needed by the live path does not automatically satisfy the other two call sites' shape, which is exactly why the founder had to add the same field in two places today to pass typecheck; this will recur for every new metadata field.
duplicates.recommendation: Standardize on web-chat-store.ts's MessageMetadata (already the live write-path shape) and have the other two extend/import it or be renamed so the shared name stops implying interchangeability.

duplicates.what: Artifacts gallery (desktop)
duplicates.liveCopy: apps/desktop/src/features/v3/AgiWorkArtifacts.tsx (mounted at DesktopShellV3.tsx:854)
duplicates.evidence: ArtifactsGallery.tsx is exported only from apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/index.ts, and grep confirms zero other files import that barrel and zero '<ArtifactsGallery' JSX usage anywhere outside its own file/tests. Its sole dependent, ArtifactCategoryFilter.tsx, is dead for the same reason. It is not in the vite.config.ts-excluded archive/ directory, so it still ships in the build despite rendering nowhere.
duplicates.driftRisk: None functionally (unreachable), but it can mislead an engineer into editing the wrong gallery implementation, and it silently ships dead weight in the bundle.
duplicates.recommendation: Delete ArtifactsGallery.tsx and ArtifactCategoryFilter.tsx, or move them into archive/ (already build-excluded) if kept for reference. Zero-risk given zero live importers.

duplicates.what: Public + in-app Gallery page
copies: apps/web/app/gallery/GalleryClient.tsx (single implementation, two route mounts: apps/web/app/gallery/page.tsx and apps/web/app/chat/artifacts/page.tsx)
duplicates.liveCopy: both routes render the same file
duplicates.evidence: apps/web/app/chat/artifacts/page.tsx's own doc comment: 'the surface gets two mounts of ONE component... There is no forked copy — a change to the gallery lands on both.' Confirmed both routes import the identical GalleryClient.tsx.
duplicates.recommendation: No action — this is the correct pattern (public SEO page + in-app page sharing one component) and should be the template for the project-gallery duplication below.

duplicates.what: Project gallery / list
duplicates.liveCopy: web: ProjectGallery (via apps/web/app/chat/projects/page.tsx); desktop: AgiWorkProjects.tsx (via DesktopShellV3.tsx:815 and :882) — both live, independently
duplicates.evidence: ProjectGallery.tsx (452 lines) is imported only by apps/web/app/chat/projects/page.tsx; AgiWorkProjects.tsx (462 lines) is imported/mounted twice in DesktopShellV3.tsx and reads a completely separate store (apps/desktop/src/stores/projectStore.ts) with no relation to whatever backs ProjectGallery. No doc comment on AgiWorkProjects.tsx explains why it isn't the shared component with a desktop transport (unlike DesktopLibrary.tsx, which does explain this for Library).

axis: Settings and navigation — duplicated definitions and duplicate entry points
summary: The nav-rail extraction into app-nav-items.ts is real and correctly adopted by its two original targets (WebChatPage, WebAppShell), but a third, independently hand-rolled nav model survives and is LIVE: WebSidebar.tsx (v3), mounted by CloudCodePage at /chat/code — one of the eight destinations on the very rail app-nav-items.ts centralized. It shows only 2 items instead of 8 when expanded, and its own collapsed state shows more links than its expanded state (self-inconsistency). Settings is architecturally sound: /settings/* routes are almost all deliberate SettingsModalRedirect shims into one canonical WebSettingsModal + packages/ui SettingsModal shell — not a duplicate UI. But two route folders (byok, sync) are real standalone pages with zero equivalent in the modal and zero in-app discovery path (the exact "setting in one place but not the other" the task asked to find); a third (voice) had the identical gap until a same-day fix wired it into the modal, which is good evidence for how to fix byok/sync too. Account deletion is duplicated and already drifted in a way that matters: AccountSection.tsx and PrivacySection.tsx both independently implement "Delete account" against the same endpoint, but only AccountSection signs the user out afterward — PrivacySection leaves a fully authenticated client session after the account is server-side scheduled for erasure. A third, dead copy in UserSettings.tsx hits a different endpoint entirely (data-only erasure that explicitly keeps the login) while its UI claims full account deletion, which would resurface a compliance-relevant mislabel if that dead page were ever wired back up.

Not applied — this is a product-scope decision (code page's nav is deliberately narrower today), flagging with evidence rather than silently rewriting.

Already diverged: AccountSection.handleDeleteSuccessContinue (lines 230-245) calls logout() + clerkSignOut({redirectUrl:'/'}) after success; PrivacySection's handleDeleteAccount never calls logout or clerkSignOut anywhere in the file — it only sets deleteSuccess=true and shows a static message (lines 797-801), leaving the user's client session authenticated after the account is scheduled for server-side erasure. Zero test coverage for either flow (grepped all .test.tsx files for 'Delete account'/handleDeleteAccount/delete-account: no hits).
duplicates.recommendation: Collapse to one implementation (shared hook/component rendered from both tabs) or cross-link Privacy's danger zone to Account's delete flow the way SecuritySection.tsx:147 already cross-links to Account for session management instead of re-implementing it. Not deleted here — both are live and the correct UX (dialog+forced-signout vs inline+no-signout) is a product decision, not a cleanup call.

axis: Extension marketplaces — Plugins / Skills / Connectors / Marketplace / Apps / Integrations
summary: Of 12 top-level routes plus 3 /features/* spurs, only /apps, /skills, /connectors are real front doors (the global nav only links /apps); the rest are thin redirects, honestly-scoped marketing pages, or one orphaned dead page. The actual defect isn't route sprawl — it's that /connectors has two independently-coded full implementations of 'browse/connect/add a connector' (the standalone ConnectorsPage.tsx and the settings-modal's ConnectorsPanel), and they have already drifted: a password-autofill security fix (CONNECTOR-FORM-PASSWORD-AUTOFILL-01) landed in only one copy, disconnect-confirmation exists in only one copy, and today's uncommitted diff is adding a new competitive-parity JSON-import feature exclusively to the copy signed-in users never see. A near-identical pattern (copy-pasted confirm dialog, tracked live in today's diff) is happening inside the settings-modal file itself between DirectoryBrowse and PluginsPanel. /skills/[name] is a fully separate, unreachable detail page whose category-label function has already diverged from the modal's equivalent. /plugins and /apps→Plugins-tab are a deliberate, correctly-cross-linked split (public catalogue vs product lifecycle); /features/plugins vs /plugins tell contradictory 'is this real yet' stories with no link between them.

duplicates.what: Browse/connect/add/disconnect a connector — full interactive implementation
duplicates.liveCopy: packages/ui/ui/src/settings-modal/SettingsModal.tsx ConnectorsPanel, via apps/web/features/settings/components/WebSettingsModal.tsx — this is what every signed-in user hits. ConnectorsPage.tsx only renders for signed-out visitors / the brief Clerk-loading window (apps/web/app/connectors/page.tsx:14-37), and its isSignedIn-gated features (e.g. the 'Inspect MCP server' button at ConnectorsPage.tsx:328) can never actually fire because that condition never coincides with the component being on screen.
duplicates.driftRisk: Proven, not hypothetical: (1) the modal's AddCustomConnectorForm has a documented password-autofill fix (autoComplete=new-password, data-1p-ignore/lpignore/bwignore) that ConnectorsPage's InspectMcpServerDialog auth-token field (ConnectorsPage.tsx:335-341) never received — same vulnerability, unfixed in the other copy, currently dormant only because of routing, reactivates the moment the isSignedIn gate or route mounting changes. (2) ConnectorsPage gates Disconnect behind a confirm Dialog; the modal's ConnectorsPanel.handleDisconnect (SettingsModal.tsx:392-395,1339) fires with no confirmation at all — same destructive action, inconsistent safety UX depending which copy renders. (3) Today's uncommitted diff adds a new 'paste MCP config as JSON' import feature (parseCustomMcpJsonConfig, new file apps/web/features/connectors/lib/custom-mcp-json-import.ts, comment cites 'Manus's Import MCP by JSON') exclusively to ConnectorsPage.tsx — the copy real users don't see — while the modal's AddCustomConnectorForm has zero references to it.
duplicates.evidence: apps/web/app/connectors/page.tsx:14-37 (routing split); ConnectorsPage.tsx:328 (isSignedIn-gated Inspect button), :335-341 (unhardened password field); SettingsModal.tsx:1130ish (CONNECTOR-FORM-PASSWORD-AUTOFILL-01 hardened field), :392-395 & :1339 (unconfirmed disconnect); both import CONNECTORS from apps/web/features/connectors/data/connectors.ts (shared data, divergent UI code); git status shows both files uncommitted today with the JSON-import feature landing only in ConnectorsPage.tsx.
duplicates.recommendation: Make the modal's ConnectorsPanel/AddCustomConnectorForm canonical; either render it from ConnectorsPage.tsx in a logged-out-safe mode, or strip ConnectorsPage.tsx down to non-interactive marketing content. Port the autofill fix and a consistent confirm-before-disconnect policy across both immediately, and put the new JSON-import feature into the modal (the surface users actually reach) before shipping it.
